title: HNSW Deleted-Vector Tombstones & Recall Degradation
prompt: Your enterprise RAG vector service indexes 12 million 1536-dim embeddings in an HNSW collection (M=16, efConstruction=128, efSearch=64). Every night, a document sync job deletes and re-upserts ~1.5 million changed chunks. Over two weeks, Recall@10 has degraded from 0.96 to 0.61 and p99 query latency spiked from 12 ms to 140 ms, even though active live vector count is still 12 million. Diagnose why HNSW degrades under heavy churn and design a zero-downtime compaction and re-indexing architecture.

spark.summary: HNSW soft-deletes leave tombstone nodes in the graph that trap efSearch beams in dead ends; fix it with inline tombstone-aware traversal, thresholded background segment compaction, and atomic blue-green index swaps.
spark.keyTakeaway: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, track tombstone ratio per HNSW segment and trigger background compaction + atomic swap before tombstones exceed 15–20%.
spark.byteSummary:
In-place deletion in an HNSW graph is expensive because removing a node requires rewiring up to 2*M bidirectional edges across multiple layers under write locks. To keep mutations fast, vector engines mark deleted vectors as **tombstones** (soft deletes) in a bitset and skip returning them in final results.

Under heavy daily churn (1.5M deletes/day on 12M live vectors), tombstones quickly exceed 40–50% of all graph nodes. Queries still traverse dead tombstone nodes to reach neighbors, wasting efSearch beam capacity on non-returnable nodes, fragmenting bridges between clusters, and collapsing Recall@10 from 0.96 to 0.61 while inflating hop counts and p99 latency to 140 ms.

Zero-downtime remediation combines three defenses: (1) use **segmented HNSW** (multiple immutable/appendable segments like Lucene/Qdrant) rather than one monolithic graph, (2) run **background segment compaction** when `tombstone_ratio > 0.20` to build a clean graph of live vectors only, and (3) perform an **atomic pointer/alias swap** with bounded retry and rollback if recall validation fails.

The core trade-off is background CPU/RAM headroom during compaction versus query-time recall and latency: reserving 25–30% CPU/RAM headroom for async segment merges prevents foreground p99 spikes while sustaining >96% Recall@10 indefinitely.

learningJourney.title: Why HNSW Uses Soft-Delete Tombstones Instead of Edge Rewiring
learningJourney.purpose: Explain the concurrency and graph-connectivity reasons vector engines defer physical node removal.

explanation.foundation: Physically deleting a node from an HNSW graph requires finding every incoming edge across Layers 0..L and running `SelectNeighborsHeuristic` on each affected neighbor to repair connectivity. Under concurrent read/write traffic, acquiring multi-node graph locks stalls queries.
explanation.core: Instead, engines mark `deleted[node_id] = 1` in a bitset. After 14 days of 1.5M daily updates (each update = 1 tombstone + 1 new node), your 12M-live-vector index actually holds **33M total graph nodes**, of which **63% are dead tombstones**.

learningJourney.title: How Tombstones Starve efSearch and Collapse Recall@10
learningJourney.purpose: Trace why efSearch=64 returns poor results and high latency when half the graph is dead.

explanation.foundation: During Layer 0 beam search, `efSearch = 64` caps the candidate frontier. When 63% of visited nodes are tombstones:
explanation.core:
- **Beam Pollution**: Half the `efSearch` slots fill with dead nodes that must be traversed to keep graph paths connected, leaving far fewer live candidates.
- **Broken Express Bridges**: Upper-layer hub nodes marked deleted can no longer be returned, and if their live neighbors were pruned earlier, the beam gets trapped in suboptimal local minima (`Recall@10: 0.96 -> 0.61`).
- **Latency Spike**: The engine must expand deeper hops and still misses `K=10` live matches, pushing p99 from `12 ms` to `140 ms`.

learningJourney.title: Segmented HNSW Indexing & Thresholded Background Compaction
learningJourney.purpose: Replace a single monolithic HNSW graph with bounded segments that compact independently.

explanation.foundation: Rather than one 12M-node graph, partition the collection into **8–16 bounded segments** (e.g., 1M–1.5M vectors each, similar to Qdrant/Milvus/Lucene):
explanation.core:
1. **Tombstone Ratio Metric**: Track `tombstone_ratio = deleted_count / total_nodes` per segment.
2. **Compaction Trigger (`> 20%`)**: When a segment crosses 20% tombstones, a background worker reads *only live vectors* from that segment and builds a fresh HNSW sub-graph (`M=16, efConstruction=128`) on isolated CPU cores.
3. **Atomic Segment Swap**: Once built and verified, swap the segment pointer atomically in memory and free the old segment after active readers drain.

learningJourney.title: Content-Hash Diffing to Cut Unnecessary Churn by 70–85%
learningJourney.purpose: Prevent nightly sync jobs from deleting and re-inserting unchanged document chunks.

explanation.foundation: Many RAG pipelines blindly `delete_by_doc_id` + `insert` all chunks when a document's metadata updates. Adding a deterministic **SHA-256 content hash** per chunk lets the sync worker skip unchanged embeddings:
explanation.core:
- Compare `(chunk_id, content_sha256)` against stored payload metadata.
- Only delete removed chunks and insert modified chunks—cutting daily tombstone generation from 1.5M to ~200K.

learningJourney.purpose: Implement a production compaction controller with bounded retry, canary recall check, and rollback.

learningJourney.title: Preventing Compaction CPU & Memory Contention on Live Traffic
learningJourney.purpose: Size cluster headroom and cgroup/thread limits so HNSW rebuilds never spike foreground p99.

explanation.foundation: Building an HNSW graph (`efConstruction=128`) is heavily CPU- and memory-bandwidth-intensive. Running compaction on all cores alongside peak RAG traffic will spike p99 latency:
explanation.core:
- **Thread Pool Cap**: Limit HNSW builder threads to `25%` of host vCPUs (e.g., 4 of 16 cores) and nice priority.
- **Memory Headroom**: Reserve `30%` free RAM above the 12M live index size so shadow segment construction never triggers OS swap.
- **Staggered Segment Merging**: Compact at most 1 segment per shard concurrently.

learningJourney.title: Tracking Tombstone Ratio, Effective efSearch, and Recall SLOs
learningJourney.purpose: Define Prometheus alerts and automated golden-set recall probes to catch graph decay early.

explanation.foundation: Monitor three leading indicators so Recall@10 never silently drops again:
explanation.core:
- **`hnsw_segment_tombstone_ratio`**: Alert at `> 0.25` (indicates compaction is falling behind churn).
- **`hnsw_nodes_visited_per_query`**: Rising hop counts at constant `efSearch` signal dead-node detours before p99 breaches.
- **Synthetic Golden Recall Probe**: Run 100 fixed ground-truth queries against exact flat k-NN hourly and alert if `Recall@10 < 0.94`.
